flows.name: One chat turn
flows.what: One owner message in the web UI, through the model and its tools, until every step is in durable history.

steps.name: Owner sends a message
steps.what: The owner types in an open chat; the browser posts the message detached and keeps following the chat's live feed, which carries everything the turn emits.
steps.in: message text typed in an open chat
steps.out: 202 started · the turn runs in its own goroutine

files.note: The chat's live feed and the followed approver
The chat store that sends and follows

children.name: Follow the chat feed
children.what: Every open tab already streams the chat's feed: first a replay of the running turn's frames, then each new frame as it is published.
children.out: SSE: feed_state, delta, tool_call, approval_request, turn_done…

children.name: Post the message
children.what: The chat store posts the text with detach: true, so the request returns at once and the answer arrives on the feed instead.

children.name: Cross-site guard
children.what: Rejects anything that is not JSON, comes from a non-loopback Origin or names a non-loopback Host, so a forged browser request cannot start a turn (bash runs ungated).

flags.text: POST /api/chat (handleChat) and POST /api/approve (handleApprove) decode their bodies with json.NewDecoder(r.Body) directly: no size limit and unknown fields accepted, unlike the management routes, which use decodeManagementJSONUpTo.

children.name: Pick the chat, claim the turn
children.what: Finds the open chat the request names and registers this turn; a closed chat, a held chat, a changed model or a second send get a 409.

highlight: Chat model changed; refresh before sending

children.name: Answer 202, run detached
children.what: Answers 202 started immediately and runs the turn in a goroutine with the followed approver, so closing the tab does not stop the turn.

children.name: Hand the turn to the agent
children.what: Calls the chat agent's Session.Send; a panic ends only this turn, and a busy or lease-conflict refusal is reported on the feed.

steps.name: Pin scope, preset and tools
steps.what: When the chat opens, its Workspace's Agent Preset resolves into one immutable Toolset and a Composition Receipt stored with the session; each turn then takes the session's turn lease before it writes anything.
steps.in: Workspace + revision (at chat open), then the owner message
steps.out: agent.Session (pinned Toolset, ScopeContext) holding a fenced turn lease

children.name: Open the chat
children.what: Opening a new chat in a Workspace reads the Workspace's default Agent Preset for its current revision.

children.name: Resolve the Agent Preset
children.what: Resolves each required and optional Capability of the preset against ready plugins and adds them to the base tools, producing a Toolset and its Composition Receipt.

flags.text: ADR 0012 and the plugins spec describe user-authored presets versioned in procedural Git; ResolvePresetContext knows only the four built-ins (Standard, Research, Explore, Build) and refuses any other preset ID.
A ready plugin's capabilities reach a session only when its Agent Preset names them (resolvePreset).

children.name: Store session + receipt
children.what: Creates the Workspace session and its Composition Receipt together, after checking the preset is allowed in that Workspace revision.

children.name: Build the agent
children.what: serve builds each chat's agent.Session with the resolved Toolset, the session's ScopeContext, a history and a turn owner bound to a fresh holder ID, and the background pass as its compaction flush.

flags.text: Disabling a plugin later leaves this session's Toolset intact, because a Toolset copies its tool definitions; whether those tools still work is up to the provider's Stop.

children.name: Take the turn lease
children.what: Send takes the session's turn lease, so only one turn (or one background commit) writes to the conversation at a time, and starts a heartbeat that renews it.

flags.text: A lost lease cancels the turn with ErrLeaseLost (startHeartbeat), and every append is fenced by the lease token, so a turn that lost its lease cannot write.

children.name: Append the owner message
children.what: The owner's text becomes the turn's root event; every later event of the turn hangs off it.

steps.name: Assemble the context
steps.what: Rebuilds the model request from durable state every time: stored history, repository instructions, the standing memory block, Automatic Recall evidence and the pinned tool schemas, compacting first when it would not fit.
steps.out: ChatRequest (messages + tool schemas) + context_snapshot event

children.name: Reload durable history
children.what: Loads the stored events (on later iterations only those after the last one loaded) and validates the compaction chain, so each request reflects exactly what is stored.
children.in: session ID, events loaded so far

flags.text: A tool call cut off by cancellation or a lost lease leaves a tool_intent with no outcome; history reconstruction drops such incomplete tool-call groups (incompleteToolGroupEvents) instead of replaying them.

children.name: Repository instructions
children.what: Captures once per turn the instructions file the owner enabled for the Workspace's folder and renders it as a JSON note; a folder that changed meanwhile fails the turn.

highlight: Workspace folder changed while preparing instructions

children.name: Standing memory block
children.what: Reads the accepted always-apply memories for every request, so an approval earlier in the turn already applies to its next request.

flags.text: The standing budget counts only what the approving session sees, so a later conversation can render slightly over 500 tokens; nothing is ever truncated.

children.name: Automatic Recall
children.what: At the turn's first request, searches accepted memories and earlier conversations of the same Context Scope (two results each), plus up to two more accepted-memory searches for IDs or tokens like task-12 in the message (two each), so it holds up to six accepted-memory results and two conversation excerpts as framed evidence. The Memory flow shows how.

triggers.when: at the first model request of each turn

children.name: Compact if too big
children.what: When the request would overflow the model's window, a summarizing model call replaces older events with a stored compaction summary; a provider context-length rejection gets exactly one compact-and-retry per turn.

triggers.when: a committed compaction wakes the background memory pass

children.what: POSTs the Chat Completions request with stream: true and reads the data: lines; any line, keepalives included, counts as liveness.

flags.text: A stream that goes five minutes without any line is cancelled by the idle watchdog; there is no total timeout, so long healthy streams run as long as they need.

children.name: Deltas to the feed
children.what: Each reasoning and content fragment is published on the chat's feed; the feed keeps the frames so a tab that rejoins replays them.

children.name: Retry before output
children.what: A provider failure is retried with backoff only when no text has reached the feed yet; afterwards it ends the turn.

children.name: Commit the answer
children.what: Validates the response (no choices, or finish_reason length or error, fails the turn) and appends it as an assistant_message; with no tool calls this is the turn's durable success.

flags.text: A committed final assistant message wins over a cancellation that arrived while its append was in flight: the turn still ends as a success.

steps.name: Run the tool calls
steps.what: Each tool call is recorded as an intent, run through the session's pinned Toolset (pausing for the owner when the tool is gated), and its bounded result is stored; then the turn assembles the next request.
steps.out: tool_intent, approval?, tool outcome events

children.name: Record the intent
children.what: Appends a tool_intent event with a fresh execution ID and emits tool_call to the feed before anything runs.

children.name: Find the tool and its gate
children.what: Looks the call up in the pinned Toolset; it is gated when the tool needs approval or its RequiresApproval check says so, and an erroring check counts as yes.

flags.text: bash is deliberately ungated, with no approval and no path denylist, because a shell walks around any fence; the cross-site guard exists for that reason.

children.name: Approval handshake
children.what: For a gated call the turn pauses inside Send while the owner's answer arrives as a separate HTTP request; the decision is stored before the tool may run.

flags.text: Approval ids are no secret from local software. guard only checks for JSON, a loopback Origin and a loopback Host, so any local process passes it (the CLI's connection commands rely on that); /api/chats/follow replays the running turn's frames to such a caller, approval_request ids included (chatFeed.publish keeps every frame and follow returns them); and POST /api/approve needs nothing but that id. A local process can therefore answer a gated call. Sources: Server.guard, connectionCommands.post, Server.handleFollow, sseEvents.ApprovalRequest.

children.name: Prepare and preview
children.what: Builds the effect before asking: for edit_file, a full before-and-after preview; the turn's lease is checked first, since deciding may reach a server.

children.name: Ask on the feed
children.what: Registers a pending approval under a random 8-byte id tagged with its chat, and publishes approval_request with the tool, arguments and preview on the chat's feed.

children.name: Owner answers
children.what: The tab shows the approval card; Approve or Decline posts the id and the answer.

children.name: Claim exactly once
children.what: claimPending removes the entry under the lock, so exactly one answer wins; a late or unknown id gets 404.

children.name: Wait or expire
children.what: The approver waits for the answer; with no tab following for two minutes, or when the turn stops, it expires and the model is told the owner never saw it.

children.name: Store the decision
children.what: Appends the approval event (plus a semantic approval when the tool bound a memory proposal) before the tool may run.

flags.text: A prepared tool with semantic ApprovalMetadata fails unless an approval observer is wired, so a semantic change never runs without a durable approval record.

children.name: Run it
children.what: Re-checks the lease, then runs the prepared effect or the tool itself; a decline or expiry becomes a fixed message to the model instead.
children.out: tool text, or an error result

triggers.when: the model calls delegate_research, delegate_explore or delegate_build

children.name: Store the bounded result
children.what: Bounds the result (100 KiB for most tools), appends it under the intent or the approval as succeeded, failed or cancelled, and emits tool_result to the feed.

flows.name: Workflows
flows.what: An approved workflow from its activation and schedule ticks to a run that advances node by node and records each effect's Effect Receipt.
flows.trigger: The owner approves a definition that declares a schedule, and every schedule tick (15 s by default, the first at startup) decides its due slots; runs also start from the web (POST /api/workflows/start), the CLI (evie workflows run) and a chat's workflow_start tool.

steps.name: Approve and activate
steps.what: The owner approves exactly the proposal card they reviewed, and the store records it as the next active version, with its schedule, in one transaction.
